topic: the residual prefill gap is mixed-traffic efficiency, which TileLang does not expose

derivation.gap: the vendor sustains about 23% more mixed read+write throughput; that is the same size as the 20% time gap we see

interpretation: the isolated rates show the path itself can do 2.35 TB/s reading and 3.08 TB/s writing, so neither direction is at a hard ceiling
when both directions run together the achievable aggregate falls to 1.76-1.97 TB/s, and the vendor reaches 2.42 TB/s under the same mixed load
64 cores each streaming a 32 KB read and a 32 KB write means 128 concurrent DRAM streams; the vendor presumably arranges its traffic with better locality
TileLang exposes no knob for DRAM page locality, stream count or copy engine selection beyond the L2 policy already applied
what_this_rules_out: further tuning of tile size, pipeline depth, buffer count, accumulator count or L2 policy, all of which are measured and none of which changes the mixed-traffic rate
status: decode met; prefill 20% short and this is the reason
